hook: NASA telescopes just found 27 mysterious icy objects orbiting far beyond Neptune.

sections.voiceover: NASA telescopes just found 27 mysterious icy objects orbiting far beyond Neptune.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing Hubble and James Webb Space Telescope in orbit.
b_roll: NASA Hubble Space Telescope public domain illustration
James Webb Space Telescope public domain image

sections.voiceover: On September 14, 2026, researchers confirmed these bodies exist in the deep solar system. Each of the 27 Trans-Neptunian Objects measures less than 25 miles across. How do these tiny remnants reveal our ancient origins?
sections.visual_cue: Animation showing Neptune and the icy belt beyond it.
b_roll: Public domain diagram of the outer solar system

sections.voiceover: Except the smallest of these icy worlds is only 6 miles wide.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a small, cratered icy body.
b_roll: Public domain artist impression of a small Trans-Neptunian Object

sections.voiceover: The Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope captured these distant targets together. Scientists now plan to search for even smaller rocks just 1 kilometer wide. These observations provide vital clues about primordial solar system formation.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen of Hubble and Webb telescope lenses.
b_roll: NASA Science archival imagery of telescope operations

sections.voiceover: These 27 icy relics whisper secrets of our distant past.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the solar system fading to black.
